name: Nativism in United States politics
scope: American nativism as the defining sources present it: in Higham's words, "intense opposition to an internal minority on the ground of its foreign (i.e. 'un-American') connections" (Encyclopedia.com), whose major traditions are anti-Catholicism, antiradicalism and the cult of Anglo-Saxon superiority and whose major historical contribution has been the restriction of immigration. Periods the sources cover: the 1798 Alien and Sedition Acts, the 1830s-1850s anti-Catholic movement and the Know-Nothings, the 1880s-1920s exclusion and national-origins quota era (Chinese Exclusion Act, literacy tests, the 1921 and 1924 acts, Madison Grant's racial argument; Erika Lee), the Cold War red scares and the modern strand. Excludes European nativism and Huntington's cultural argument, which none of them names as nativism.

summary: American nativism is opposition to immigrants on the ground of their foreign connections, defended as protecting a native-born, historically Anglo-Protestant majority. Its main program is restricting immigration, and its strands include anti-Catholic conspiracy charges and the 1920s racial and eugenic argument of Madison Grant, who rejects democratic equality and the Melting Pot. The sources say little about economics or other issues.
notes: Searched the defining sources (Lee 2020, the New Catholic Encyclopedia entry) and Grant's book for each theme: immigration, race and heredity, eugenics, democracy and equality, assimilation, religion, economy, government, world. Only the positions they state are answered; the rest are null. The earlier pass's Wikipedia, 1856 platform, 1924 Act and Huntington sources stay listed only so the history of the earlier answers can cite them.
